The most serious crime he can be convicted of is involuntary manslaughter (unlawful-act manslaughter): his intent to commit a battery transfers to the teammate, but intending only a slight wound does not supply the malice needed for murder. The team note is wrong to call this mere negligence, because he deliberately fired a gun at another person, so the death results from an intentional unlawful act. Second-degree murder through felony murder is possible only if his jurisdiction treats the shooting as an inherently dangerous felony, such as aggravated battery with a firearm.

CONFIDENCE: 60
